facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is price dependence. The average realized gold price was USD 2,156 per ounce in FY2024, USD 3,184 in FY2025 and USD 4,140 in the first nine months of 2026, and total debt to EBITDA was 1.95x at 2024-12-31, so the net cash position rests on prices that have nearly doubled. A fall toward FY2024 prices would compress EBITDA while the 2029 and 2032 notes stay fixed. Cash interest for the latest twelve months and the exact 2029 notes principal would settle the two open items in the metrics; a lower realized price would be the signal that changes the view. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C4

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 117; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23 - Cells the filings print as a dash are missing values and are marked not supplied: fair value adjustments in several periods, the Silvertip and Other segment revenue lines, goodwill at FY2024, the issuance of notes in 9M 2026 and Q3 2026, and the dividend, performance share settlement and investment purchase lines in periods with no such activity. The sale of investments and proceeds from notes receivable lines, which print dashes for FY2024 and FY2025, are not carried. A line that a statement does not print for a period, such as the loss on disposal of assets in the quarterly statements or share repurchases in FY2024, is likewise marked not supplied. Severity is low. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 129–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4 - The long-term stockpile is not shown apart from Other non-current assets at 2024-12-31, and deferred tax assets are shown apart only in the later annual report, so line-level comparison of those lines across periods is limited. Totals are unaffected. Severity is low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 152 - Per-share amounts, other comprehensive income lines and the segment costs and income from operations printed in the segment note are not carried in the statement tables, which carry the issuer's income statement lines and segment revenue. Severity is low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 and 12–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130 and 147–148 - The dividend declared on 2026-11-04 has no stated total, and the insurance proceeds of USD 70 million are expected in the fourth quarter and not received, so the post-balance-sheet table states one pro forma row and one gap. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a strong profile is that the cushion was built by price. Net cash and 63.84% conversion of adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow rest on realized gold of USD 4,140 per ounce in the nine months, while the FY2024 average was USD 2,156 and the issuer's own guidance assumes USD 4,000 per ounce. At the FY2025 average prices the nine-month adjusted EBITDA would fall 60.31% to USD 556,043 thousand, a margin of 26.73% against 47.89% before the price effect, and the small hedge book gives little protection. A second guidance cut, a lapse of the Las Chispas permit, or debt-funded distributions would move the view toward average; a full year of the Canadian mines at planned output with stable unit costs would confirm it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation A2; calculation A9

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Coeur is a precious metals producer with seven wholly-owned mines in the United States, Canada and Mexico, and gold, silver and copper supplied 62.35%, 32.54% and 5.11% of the nine-month revenue of USD 2,925,400 thousand. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Coeur presents a strong business profile on the evidence supplied, with no peer data to rank it, supported by seven mines in three countries, net cash and a cash conversion of 63.84%, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on gold and silver prices, a still unproven ramp-up of two acquired mines and a note structure that leaves Mexican revenue outside the guarantors. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at current prices and sensitive to a price fall. Refinancing capacity depends on the 2029 notes, which cash already covers, and on the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolving facility. The primary downside path is a price fall during ramp-up combined with debt-funded distributions. Further analysis would require the financing documents, ratings, mine-level profit and cash interest for 2026. ### Bottom line

The supplied Coeur Mining filings and releases support Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit with limitations, but not a covenant, legal-document, ratings or market-pricing assessment, so lender protections rest on the issuer's own summaries.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 178–179

## Findings
### Bottom line

Coeur Mining reports net cash of USD 471,080 thousand at 2026-09-30, so net debt to EBITDA is -0.26x and creditors face no net leverage, but trailing EBITDA includes the acquired Canadian operations only from the acquisition date, so the ratio is not a like-for-like trend.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation C6; calculation C13

Debt is USD 701,652 thousand against cash of USD 1,172,732 thousand, and the USD 1,000 million revolving facility is undrawn. Pro forma for the insurance settlement agreed on 2026-10-23, net cash would be USD 541.08 million and net debt to EBITDA -0.30x. Two items are not established from the filings: cash interest paid for any 2026 period, so trailing interest cover cannot be calculated, and the outstanding principal of the 2029 notes, so the maturity ladder is incomplete.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C14; calculation C17
### Key findings

Net leverage has fallen from 1.77x at 2024-12-31 to -0.22x at 2025-12-31 and -0.26x at 2026-09-30. EBITDA rose from USD 302,600 thousand in FY2024 to USD 964,579 thousand in FY2025 while debt fell from USD 590,058 thousand to USD 340,533 thousand, so the improvement came from earnings and net repayment of debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 116–117; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C5

Cash interest paid was USD 49,806 thousand in FY2024 and USD 31,763 thousand in FY2025, which gives EBITDA cover of 6.08x and 30.37x. The quarterly reports print no cash interest, so interest cover for the latest twelve months is not calculable and the improvement cannot be extended to 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 175; 10-K_2024-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Cash from operations was USD 1,239,687 thousand in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 512,292 thousand a year earlier, and free cash flow was USD 894,491 thousand after USD 345,196 thousand of capital expenditures. Share repurchases of USD 221,232 thousand and dividends of USD 20,645 thousand took USD 241,877 thousand of that, so shareholder distributions are the largest use of cash after capital expenditures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C19; calculation C20

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is USD 1,172,732 thousand of cash and USD 972.3 million of undrawn revolving credit after USD 27.7 million of letters of credit, against USD 701,652 thousand of debt. Cash alone exceeds the carrying value of the 2029 notes, USD 291,342 thousand, so the nearest maturity in the sources is covered without drawing the facility.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; calculation C16

The latest twelve months are not on a pro forma basis. The New Gold balance sheet is in the figures at 2026-09-30, but its earnings enter EBITDA only from the acquisition date, and the issuer's pro forma note covers revenue and net income, not EBITDA. The leverage ratio at 2026-09-30 therefore sits on a part-year earnings base, which makes it conservative rather than flattering.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 22

Claims outside the debt figure are large relative to debt: reclamation obligations were USD 427,296 thousand at 2026-09-30 and deferred tax liabilities USD 3,100,085 thousand after the acquisition accounting. Only the current portion of operating lease liabilities, USD 7,664 thousand, is printed at 2026-09-30, and no pension or retiree medical obligation is disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 2 and 38; calculation C18
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is price dependence. The average realized gold price was USD 2,156 per ounce in FY2024, USD 3,184 in FY2025 and USD 4,140 in the first nine months of 2026, and total debt to EBITDA was 1.95x at 2024-12-31, so the net cash position rests on prices that have nearly doubled. A fall toward FY2024 prices would compress EBITDA while the 2029 and 2032 notes stay fixed. Cash interest for the latest twelve months and the exact 2029 notes principal would settle the two open items in the metrics; a lower realized price would be the signal that changes the view.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C4

The sale of investments and proceeds from notes receivable lines, which print dashes for FY2024 and FY2025, are not carried. A line that a statement does not print for a period, such as the loss on disposal of assets in the quarterly statements or share repurchases in FY2024, is likewise marked not supplied. Severity is low.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 129–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4

spans.text: # Business & governance: Coeur Mining, Inc.
## Request

Business and governance for Coeur Mining, Inc. (issuer cde-215466), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, transaction history and governance behaviour that bear on creditors, built from the ten supplied filings and releases.
## Sources

Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 267354b70d66d83cacc46e7ea7ff6da33c12051397117ff655b905f73d8c8d38, used for the document map, document dates and source gaps.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Coeur Mining is a North American precious-metals producer with no controlling holder identified in the supplied documents and a record of creditor-aligned financial policy, so sponsor and governance risk is low, although the missing proxy statement and financing documents bound that view.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 178–179

Two share-funded acquisitions in 2025 and 2026 turned a five-mine business into seven mines across the United States, Mexico and Canada, and no mine supplied more than 22.04% of nine-month revenue. The creditor risks sit in integration and structure, not owner conduct: the full-year gold expectation fell by 8.70% between August and November, to the low end of its range, and the Mexican mines that earned 34.95% of revenue are not among the named note guarantors.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cde_a2q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation K1; calculation K6; calculation K10
### Key findings

The business is diversified by mine, metal and country, which limits single-site outage risk but not metal-price risk. In the first nine months of 2026 no mine exceeded 22.04% of revenue, gold supplied 62.35%, silver 32.54% and copper 5.11%, and the United States, Mexico and Canada supplied 33.36%, 34.95% and 31.69%. A mine outage therefore costs a fraction of revenue, while a fall in gold or silver prices reaches 94.89% of it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K3; calculation K4

Both large acquisitions were paid in shares, so no acquisition debt entered the capital structure, but integration is now the main operating risk. The New Gold purchase price was USD 6,938,701 thousand in newly issued shares, the company assumed debt with a fair value of USD 414,767 thousand, and transaction and integration costs reached USD 39.3 million. The two Canadian mines supplied 31.69% of nine-month revenue, yet the full-year gold expectation was cut by 8.70% between August and November, to the low end of its range, in a quarter with a conveyor failure at New Afton and heavy rain at Rainy River and Palmarejo.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cde_a2q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation K2; calculation K10

No controlling holder is identified in the documents supplied, but the documents that would show board independence and holder concentration are not supplied. Holders of New Gold stock received 37.96% of the shares outstanding at 2026-03-31, the chairman also serves as chief executive, and the annual report leaves board, pay and ownership disclosure to a proxy statement that is not in the source set. Creditor risk from owner conduct cannot be tested beyond documented actions.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 178–179; calculation K7

Financial policy is conservative on leverage and generous to shareholders, which is creditor-aligned today and the main behaviour to monitor. The long-term target is zero net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA, the revolving facility was repaid by USD 195.0 million net in 2025, USD 39.5 million of finance lease principal was prepaid in 2026, and USD 221,232 thousand of share repurchases plus USD 20,645 thousand of dividends were paid in nine months. Repurchases took 46.13% of third-quarter free cash flow and USD 519.4 million of the USD 750 million authorization remains, so distributions are funded from operations while the contractual limits on them are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 60; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation K8; calculation K9

The note guarantee structure appears to leave the Mexican operations outside the guarantor group, which puts a large share of revenue behind subsidiary creditors. Summarized guarantor revenue was USD 1,902,992 thousand of USD 2,925,400 thousand, leaving USD 1,022,408 thousand or 34.95% outside the group, within USD 1 thousand of the two Mexican mines' combined USD 1,022,409 thousand. The named guarantors include no Mexican operating subsidiary, 47.14% of employees work in Mexico, and a USD 29.6 million Mexican value-added tax receivable has been written down since 2021.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation K2; calculation K6; calculation K11

Two streaming agreements take a share of production at fixed prices, which caps upside on those ounces and works like a senior claim on output. At Palmarejo, 50% of gold production is sold to a Franco-Nevada subsidiary for the lesser of USD 800 or spot per ounce, and at Rainy River 6.5% of gold and 60% of silver production go to Royal Gold at 25% of the spot price. In a price rally these ounces earn far less than the realized price, so group margins rise more slowly than prices.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 36

Disclosure quality is adequate for monitoring: the statements carry an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control, but the finance leadership changed in August. A new chief accounting officer took office on 2026-08-10, the former controller moved to an accounting role ahead of an intended retirement in early 2027, and disclosure controls were reported effective at 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 177
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a low-risk view is execution. The expectation moved from the midpoint to the low end of the guidance ranges within one quarter, quarterly silver production fell 12% year on year, and the operating permit for the Las Chispas mine, which earned 16.43% of third-quarter revenue, was set to expire in November 2026 with no later update in the filings. A further guidance cut, a lapse of that permit, or a debt-funded acceleration of the USD 750 million repurchase program would move the view toward medium risk. A proxy statement showing independent board control and financing documents that cap restricted payments would support the low reading.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K5; calculation K10
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not in the source set, so board independence, holder concentration, executive pay and related-party dealings are not established, and the low sponsor and governance reading rests on documented actions alone.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 178–179

- The credit agreement and indentures are described only in the issuer's own notes, so the exact room for dividends, repurchases, debt, liens and asset transfers is not established, and the view that distributions are creditor-safe rests on current net cash, not on documented limits.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

- The two Canadian mines have been in the group for about two quarters and the supplied filings give only a Rainy River mine life to 2035 and a New Afton resource estimate, not reserve estimates, so the finding that integration is the main operating risk rests on a short operating record and incomplete mine-life evidence.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The central transaction is the acquisition of New Gold Inc., agreed on 2025-11-02 and completed on 2026-03-20 by court-approved plan of arrangement. New Gold shareholders received a fixed fraction of a Coeur share for each New Gold share, for a purchase price of USD 6,938,701 thousand, so the deal added no acquisition debt. The preliminary allocation assigns USD 9,585,545 thousand to property, plant and equipment and USD 2,793,678 thousand to deferred tax liabilities, and leaves reclamation, unrecognized tax benefits and deferred taxes open for up to one year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

Two debt events followed. First, the company replaced its 2017 credit agreement with a new USD 1,000 million senior secured revolving facility maturing in March 2031, with no draws at 2026-09-30. Second, it exchanged USD 385.8 million of the USD 400.0 million New Gold senior notes due 2032 for USD 385,774 thousand of its own senior unsecured notes due 2032 plus USD 771,600 of cash, settled on 2026-04-22, and obtained consents that removed restrictive covenants from the notes that stayed outstanding, about USD 12.6 million at 2026-09-30. Supplemental indentures added New Gold and two related entities as guarantors of the 2029 notes on 2026-04-30 and clarified the first interest date on the 2032 notes on 2026-10-07.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; EX99.1_2026-03-31_cde_ef20071153-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

The earlier SilverCrest acquisition closed on 2025-02-14 and was also paid in shares, at an implied equity value of USD 1.58 billion, and the company repaid USD 195.0 million net under the revolving facility in 2025. Shareholder returns began in 2026 with an expanded USD 750 million repurchase program announced on 2026-03-23, an inaugural dividend of USD 0.02 per share paid on 2026-06-10 and a second dividend declared on 2026-11-04 for payment on 2026-12-16.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

spans.text: # Fundamental credit: Coeur Mining, Inc.
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Coeur Mining, Inc. (issuer cde-215466), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the overall credit profile, its strongest support and primary downside, built from the ten supplied filings and releases and the three earlier module handoffs.
## Sources

Supplied handoffs: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 267354b70d66d83cacc46e7ea7ff6da33c12051397117ff655b905f73d8c8d38; Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 4ff68a0b555bcd6436e4f6a6785a7945e4e82ba51ecce20fbf0237a045854092; Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 ea35c7140eac975bf25a49a1a063d4580fbc8829fe12ca00ea144ec5b62e889e. They supply the document map, the debt, liquidity and leverage figures, and the business, ownership and governance facts.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Coeur Mining's credit profile is strong at current metal prices, with net cash and no near-term maturity pressure, but earnings depend on gold and silver prices while two new mines ramp up, so creditors face price and execution risk, not leverage risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation R1; calculation R8

At 2026-09-30 net cash was USD 471,080 thousand and USD 972.3 million of revolving credit was undrawn; pro forma for the insurance settlement agreed on 2026-10-23, net cash is USD 541.08 million and net leverage -0.30x. Gold and silver supplied 94.89% of nine-month revenue, and reaching even the lowest full-year production expectation requires fourth-quarter gold output 29.28% above the third quarter.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation R1; calculation R2; calculation R8; calculation A11
### Key findings

Leverage is not the credit constraint. Net cash was USD 471,080 thousand at 2026-09-30 against total debt of USD 701,652 thousand, which is 0.39x trailing reported EBITDA, and net leverage was -0.26x. Pro forma for the insurance settlement agreed on 2026-10-23, net cash is USD 541.08 million and net leverage -0.30x; a pro forma cash figure is not established. Cash of USD 1,172,732 thousand exceeds the 2029 notes at a carrying value of USD 291,342 thousand, so the nearest maturity needs no refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; calculation R1; calculation R2; calculation R3; calculation R4; calculation R7

Cash generation is high at current prices and converts well. Free cash flow was USD 894,491 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, 63.84% of adjusted EBITDA, against 64.90% in FY2025 and a negative ratio in FY2024, when realized gold averaged USD 2,156 per ounce. Capital expenditure took 11.80% of revenue, and the 2026 plan still has development spending to come.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A3; calculation A4

Earnings depend on gold and silver prices, which supplied 94.89% of nine-month revenue, and most of the revenue growth came from price rather than volume. Revenue rose 109.66% year on year, realized gold rose 40.01% and silver 105.18%, gold ounces sold rose 41.78% with the acquisitions and silver ounces sold fell 2.59%. A price fall therefore reaches almost all revenue, while seven mines spread outage risk.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation A5; calculation R8

The cost base is rising and operating leverage works against the company when volumes miss. Adjusted cost per gold ounce was USD 2,191 in the nine months against USD 1,411 a year earlier, up 55.28%, and the issuer expects costs at the upper end of the ranges because output is at the low end, so a shortfall raises unit costs. The gap between realized price and adjusted cost still widened, from USD 1,546 to USD 1,949 per ounce, because price rose faster than cost.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation A6

Execution is the main operating risk. The August expectation of USD 2.3 billion of adjusted EBITDA became over USD 2 billion in November, yet reaching it needs fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA above USD 598,883 thousand against USD 447,965 thousand in the third quarter, and gold output 29.28% above the third quarter even at the low end of guidance. A second shortfall would be the clearest sign that the acquired mines are ramping up slower than planned.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_cde_a2q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation A11; calculation A12

Rainy River is the weakest unit. Its third-quarter adjusted cost was USD 2,883 per gold ounce against a realized price of USD 4,076, a gap of USD 1,193, free cash flow fell to USD 36.1 million from USD 123.1 million in the second quarter, and the cost includes USD 694 per ounce of non-cash inventory step-up. The mine contributes the largest share of revenue, so its ramp-up decides whether group margins hold.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation A7

The notes sit behind Mexican creditors on the evidence supplied. The named guarantors include no Mexican operating subsidiary, and the Mexican mines earned 34.95% of nine-month revenue and employed 47.14% of staff at the end of 2025, before the New Gold acquisition, so a large part of cash generation is not directly available to noteholders. Las Chispas alone earned USD 124.7 million of metal sales less costs applicable to sales in the third quarter, 27.84% of group adjusted EBITDA, and its operating permit was set to expire in November 2026.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation R8; calculation A8

Financial policy is creditor-aligned today and distributions are the behaviour to watch. The stated target is zero net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA, and distributions of USD 241,877 thousand in nine months were 27.04% of free cash flow, with USD 519.4 million of the USD 750 million repurchase authorization left. A debt-funded acceleration would change the reading, and the legal limits on distributions are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation R9

The downside strains earnings and distributions before it strains liquidity. Applying the FY2025 average realized prices to nine-month volumes removes USD 845,074 thousand of revenue, 28.89% of the total and 60.31% of adjusted EBITDA, yet liquidity of cash and undrawn revolver covers that effect 2.54 times.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation A9; calculation R5
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a strong profile is that the cushion was built by price. Net cash and 63.84% conversion of adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow rest on realized gold of USD 4,140 per ounce in the nine months, while the FY2024 average was USD 2,156 and the issuer's own guidance assumes USD 4,000 per ounce. At the FY2025 average prices the nine-month adjusted EBITDA would fall 60.31% to USD 556,043 thousand, a margin of 26.73% against 47.89% before the price effect, and the small hedge book gives little protection. A second guidance cut, a lapse of the Las Chispas permit, or debt-funded distributions would move the view toward average; a full year of the Canadian mines at planned output with stable unit costs would confirm it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation A2; calculation A9
### Limitations

- The finding that margins are resilient rests on consolidated unit costs and the guidance ranges, because mine-level profit is not carried into this analysis, so a weak mine such as Rainy River could be masked or its weakness overstated.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16

- The price sensitivity applies printed prices and nine-month volumes with costs, streams, hedges and taxes held constant, so it overstates the revenue effect on streamed ounces and ignores the tax cushion, and the finding that liquidity covers the effect holds only on those terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026, so interest cover here uses income-statement interest expense, and the finding that debt service is comfortable would weaken if cash interest ran well above expense.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 3

- No ratings, market prices or peer set are supplied, so the profile is judged against the issuer's own history and its own guidance assumptions, which limits the finding that it is strong to an absolute reading rather than a ranking.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16

- Whether the implied fourth-quarter step-up in output is achievable cannot be checked against mine plans, so the execution finding rests on arithmetic from management statements and may prove too cautious or too optimistic.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths are net cash with a further USD 972.3 million of undrawn revolving credit, free cash flow of 63.84% of adjusted EBITDA, spread across seven mines with none above 22.04% of nine-month revenue, a zero net debt policy target, and no material maturity before 2029. Each one lowers default and refinancing risk because it widens the cushion between cash generation and fixed claims.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation R5; calculation A3; calculation R8

The main weaknesses are dependence on gold and silver prices for 94.89% of revenue, a ramp-up that still needs fourth-quarter output well above the third quarter, unit costs that rise when volumes fall short, notes whose named guarantors exclude the Mexican mines, and distributions whose legal limits are not established. Each one can reduce cash generation or move cash away from noteholders faster than debt reduces.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation R8; calculation A6; calculation A11

### Source gate and module status

Module status is full run with limitations: every gating source is supplied, the three earlier modules are complete, and the gaps listed under the gaps section restrict only the legal, rating and peer reading. Net debt, liquidity and leverage are taken from Financial foundation and re-stated in the calculations; business, ownership and governance facts are taken from Business & governance.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Company description

Coeur is a precious metals producer with seven wholly-owned mines in the United States, Canada and Mexico, and gold, silver and copper supplied 62.35%, 32.54% and 5.11% of the nine-month revenue of USD 2,925,400 thousand. Revenue comes from selling bullion and concentrate at market prices, so it has no contracted price and visibility depends on production and on prices. One mine, Kensington, sells its gold concentrate under a long-term offtake, which was about 18% of metal sales in 2025. The 2025 and 2026 acquisitions of SilverCrest and New Gold took the group from five mines to seven, which raised scale and diversification at the cost of integration risk.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 150; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation R8
### Ownership and group structure

Coeur is a listed company with no controlling holder identified in the supplied documents, so there is no sponsor to extract value, and former New Gold holders received 37.96% of the shares outstanding at 2026-03-31. The notes are guaranteed by named subsidiaries that exclude the Mexican operating companies, which earned 34.95% of nine-month revenue, and the revolving facility is secured by a pledge of subsidiary shares that falls away at two investment-grade ratings. The proxy statement and financing documents are not supplied, so board independence and the room for distributions are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation R8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is price times volume with no pricing power: the company sells at market prices, and the nine-month rise of 109.66% combined a 40.01% higher realized gold price, a 105.18% higher silver price and the added mines. Silver ounces sold fell 2.59% while silver revenue nearly doubled, so earnings are exposed to a silver price reversal as well as gold. Revenue is therefore cyclical with the metal price, concentrated in two metals and spread across seven mines.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation A5

Two streaming agreements cap the price on part of the output: Palmarejo sells 50% of its gold to a Franco-Nevada subsidiary at the lesser of USD 800 or spot per ounce, and Rainy River delivers 6.5% of gold and 60% of silver to Royal Gold at 25% of the spot price. In a rally those ounces earn less than the realized price, and in a fall the Palmarejo ounces fall less, which damps the price sensitivity shown later.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Mining costs are largely fixed in the short run, so volume shortfalls raise unit costs, as the issuer's own guidance shows: output at the low end leads to costs at the upper end of the ranges. Reported EBITDA margin was 47.29% in the nine months against 46.60% in FY2025 and 28.71% in FY2024, and costs applicable to sales include a non-cash inventory step-up from the acquisitions of USD 265,835 thousand in the nine months, which the cash flow statement adds back. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure at current prices, but the FY2024 margin at a realized gold price of USD 2,156 per ounce was far lower than in FY2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A6; calculation A10
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital expenditure was 11.80% of revenue in the nine months and 10.68% in FY2025, and the 2026 plan is USD 360 million to USD 405 million of sustaining and USD 160 million to USD 200 million of development capital, with spending trending to the low end. Free cash flow was 63.84% of adjusted EBITDA in the nine months, and cash taxes are guided to USD 350 million to USD 450 million for the year. The conversion is durable while prices hold, and discretionary growth capital gives some flexibility to protect cash if prices fall.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation A3; calculation A4
### Competitive forces

Rivalry in gold and silver is price-based, because output is a commodity sold at spot, so competitive position shows up only in unit cost, and no cost-curve or market-share data are supplied. New entrants face permitting and capital barriers, which the permit amendment at Las Chispas and the Rochester expansion permits illustrate. Buyers of doré are banks and refiners, while Kensington concentrate depends on third-party smelters, so a smelter failure is a counterparty risk. Suppliers of power, labour and equipment matter through inflation and tariffs, which the issuer lists among its risks.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 90
### Macro, FX and regulatory factors

Two outside factors alter credit quality. The metal price is the dominant economic driver, and the guidance assumes USD 4,000 per ounce of gold, USD 55.00 per ounce of silver, CAD 1.38 and MXN 18.00 per US dollar, so currency moves change costs at the Canadian and Mexican mines and no currency hedge was outstanding at 2026-09-30. Regulation matters through the Mexican tax and permitting record: a USD 29.6 million value-added tax receivable has been written down since 2021 and recovery depends on arbitration. Social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the materials supplied.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 75
### Credit SWOT

Strengths are net cash, 63.84% cash conversion, diversification by mine and metal, and a no-sponsor structure. Weaknesses are price dependence, rising unit costs, a Rainy River ramp-up with a thin gap between price and cost, and Mexican revenue outside the guarantors. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the Rainy River mine life extension to 2035, the New Afton K-Zone resource and a full year of the Canadian mines in 2027. Threats are a price fall during ramp-up, a lapse of the Las Chispas permit, and debt-funded distributions.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 37; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation A7; calculation R8
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is strong on leverage and liquidity and average on earnings stability. Total debt of USD 701,652 thousand is 0.39x trailing reported EBITDA and net cash was USD 471,080 thousand at 2026-09-30; pro forma for the insurance settlement agreed on 2026-10-23, net cash is USD 541.08 million and net leverage -0.30x, and a pro forma cash figure is not established. Reported EBITDA covered interest expense 48.91 times in the nine months, against 31.17 times in FY2025 and 5.90 times in FY2024, although cash interest for 2026 is not printed. The trend is sharply upward, but it follows the price, so the main missing datapoints are mine-level profit, cash interest and the financing terms.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation R1; calculation R2; calculation R4; calculation A10
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are a full year of the Canadian mines in 2027, the USD 70 million of Wharf insurance proceeds expected in the fourth quarter, and capital expenditure trending to the low end of guidance; the headwinds are production at the low end, unit costs at the upper end, and a fourth-quarter plan that needs output 29.28% above the third quarter. Management expects adjusted EBITDA above USD 2 billion and free cash flow above USD 1.3 billion for 2026 at current prices, which is management language that depends on that step-up. Over three to five years the mine-life evidence is supportive, with Rainy River extended to 2035 and Kensington held at a five-year reserve-based life, but streams at Palmarejo and Rainy River keep limiting upside.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation A11; calculation A12
### Downside scenario

The primary downside is a return of realized prices to their FY2025 averages while the two new mines are still ramping up. The first break is revenue: on nine-month volumes the lower prices remove USD 421,221 thousand from gold and USD 423,853 thousand from silver, USD 845,074 thousand in total and 28.89% of revenue, which cuts adjusted EBITDA by 60.31% to USD 556,043 thousand and the margin to 26.73%. Unit costs would then be spread over lower revenue at Rainy River, where the gap between price and cost was USD 1,193 per ounce at the third-quarter price, and the cost would rise further if silver by-product credits shrink.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_cde.htm.jsonl, page 85; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation A9; calculation A7

Free cash flow falls faster than EBITDA because development capital expenditure of USD 160 million to USD 200 million is already planned, so the management levers are slower buybacks, which took 46.13% of third-quarter free cash flow, and trimmed development and exploration spending. Liquidity covers the revenue effect 2.54 times and total debt would stay at USD 701,652 thousand against net cash, so a liquidity or refinancing problem is not indicated unless debt-funded distributions or a permit lapse at Las Chispas, whose third-quarter metal sales less costs applicable to sales were USD 124.7 million, were added to the price fall.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cde_a3q26earningsreleaseex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation A8; calculation A9; calculation R5; calculation R9
### Overall credit view

Overall, Coeur presents a strong business profile on the evidence supplied, with no peer data to rank it, supported by seven mines in three countries, net cash and a cash conversion of 63.84%, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on gold and silver prices, a still unproven ramp-up of two acquired mines and a note structure that leaves Mexican revenue outside the guarantors. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at current prices and sensitive to a price fall. Refinancing capacity depends on the 2029 notes, which cash already covers, and on the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolving facility. The primary downside path is a price fall during ramp-up combined with debt-funded distributions. Further analysis would require the financing documents, ratings, mine-level profit and cash interest for 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cde.htm.jsonl, page 21
Top risk: a fall in gold and silver prices while the Canadian mines are still ramping up.
